articles.title: Broken Promises: RIP Instagram’s End-to-End Encrypted DMs
articles.summary: Microsoft patches a staggering 167 vulns including a SharePoint zero-day and the deliciously-named 'BlueHammer' Windows Defender flaw. When your monthly patch count hits triple digits, maybe it's time to rethink some architectural choices.

articles.title: Anti-DDoS Firm Heaped Attacks on Brazilian ISPs
articles.summary: Canvas gets pwned, disrupting education nationwide as ransomware crews deface login pages with extortion demands. Nothing says 'back to school' like having your entire learning platform held hostage by cybercriminals.

articles.title: State of ransomware in 2026
articles.summary: Google catches the first AI-generated zero-day exploit in the wild, targeting 2FA in Python. The robots are learning to hack faster than we expected—and they're surprisingly bad at faking CVSS scores.

articles.title: Canada’s Bill C-22 Is a Repackaged Version of Last Year’s Surveillance Nightmare
articles.summary: EFF drops a hacker's guide to circumventing internet shutdowns because when authoritarians pull the plug, the show must go on. Essential reading for anyone who believes connectivity is a human right.

articles.title: Patch Tuesday, April 2026 Edition
articles.summary: Scattered Spider's 'Tylerb' pleads guilty to wire fraud and identity theft after SMS phishing campaigns. Another reminder that even the most sophisticated social engineering crews eventually meet their match in federal prosecutors.

articles.title: Victory! End-to-End Encrypted RCS Comes to Apple and Android Chats
articles.summary: Instagram kills its barely-used E2E encryption feature, breaking years-old promises to users. Meta proves once again that surveillance capitalism and privacy protection are fundamentally incompatible business models.

articles.title: Vietnam to develop domestic cloud so it can ditch risky overseas operators for government workloads
articles.summary: TeamPCP open-sources their Shai-Hulud worm on GitHub, because apparently even malware crews believe in transparency. Microsoft's code repository somehow missed this delightful contribution to the supply chain threat landscape.

articles.title: New TrickMo Variant Uses TON C2 and SOCKS5 to Create Android Network Pivots
articles.summary: RubyGems suspends new signups after hundreds of malicious packages flood the repository in a coordinated attack. The gems weren't the only things getting cut—so was user trust in package manager security.

articles.title: Canvas breach spotlights cybercriminal appetite for student data
articles.summary: CheckMarx's official Jenkins plugin gets compromised with infostealer malware, proving that even security companies aren't immune to supply chain attacks. The irony is so thick you could patch it with a CVE.

articles.title: It's Patch Tuesday for Microsoft and Not a Zero-Day In Sight
articles.summary: Canada repackages last year's surveillance nightmare as Bill C-22, hoping nobody notices it's the same digital rights destruction with a fresh coat of legislative paint. Spoiler alert: the privacy community noticed.
